source_type_decision.reason: Both source rows ask how to avoid or handle duplicate Kafka consumption. A scenario contract is appropriate because the answer must explain the failure window, choose offset/idempotency/transaction boundaries, cover rebalance and retry behavior, define external side-effect handling, size the deduplication state, and specify observability and fault-injection validation.

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 Consumer Configs
verified_claims: enable.auto.commit periodically commits offsets in the background and defaults to true
isolation.level=read_committed returns committed transactional data and withholds open or aborted transactional data according to last-stable-offset semantics
max.poll.interval.ms bounds the allowed delay between polls for group-managed consumers and max.poll.records bounds the records returned per poll

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.1.2 KafkaConsumer API
verified_claims: consumer position and committed position are distinct, and the committed position is the recovery point after restart
a committed offset should be the next record the application will consume
KafkaConsumer is not thread-safe and decoupled processing requires explicit offset coordination so commits do not get ahead of completed work
commitAsync is non-blocking and commit errors are passed to the callback when provided or discarded when no callback is supplied

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 Producer Configs
verified_claims: enable.idempotence defaults to true when no conflicting configuration disables it
idempotence requires acks=all, retries greater than zero, and max.in.flight.requests.per.connection less than or equal to five
transactional.id implies idempotence and enables transactional delivery semantics

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.1.2 KafkaProducer API
verified_claims: application-level re-sends are outside the producer's idempotent retry de-duplication and idempotence is guaranteed only within a producer session
sendOffsetsToTransaction marks offsets as part of the current transaction, and those offsets are committed only if the transaction commits successfully
sendOffsetsToTransaction is intended for consume-transform-produce and the committed offset is the next message to consume

primary_sources_checked.title: Apache Kafka 4.1 Design: Message Delivery Semantics and Transactions
verified_claims: Kafka's default delivery model is at-least-once, so redelivery can occur
transactional producer plus read-committed consumer provides exactly-once processing for reading, processing and writing Kafka topics
exactly-once behavior for external destination systems generally requires cooperation with those systems rather than being automatically included in the Kafka transaction
